title: Onboarding CRO: Time-to-value, activation and the psychology behind first-run experience
summary: Corey's onboarding playbook focuses on getting users to their aha moment fast. It covers minimum path to value, onboarding psychology (endowed progress, Peak-End, Fogg), checklists and empty states, and defining activation by cohort analysis. It also covers measuring success by lead-to-customer conversion and 90-day retention.

principles.text: Remove every step between signup and core value; design the minimum path to value.
principles.quote: Remove every step between signup and experiencing core value. Design the **Minimum Path to Value (MPTV)**

principles.text: Focus the first session on one successful outcome; save advanced features for later.
principles.quote: Focus first session on one successful outcome. Save advanced features for later.

principles.text: Prefer interactive doing over tutorials; users learn by doing the thing.
principles.quote: Interactive > Tutorial. Doing the thing > Learning about the thing.

principles.text: Pre-complete a checklist step to give users a head start; it lifts completion by roughly 40%.
principles.quote: A checklist that opens at "20% done" (a step pre-completed on their behalf) drives roughly **+40% completion** vs. starting at 0%.

principles.text: Judge activation by lead-to-customer conversion and 90-day retention, not signup volume.
principles.quote: **Judge activation by lead→customer conversion + 90-day retention, not lead volume.**

principles.text: A behavior needs motivation, ability and a prompt together; diagnose which is missing when a step stalls.
principles.quote: a behavior happens only when **Motivation × Ability × Prompt** converge at the same moment.
